stem.en: In early 2020, face masks suddenly sold at much higher prices. Which explanation fits best?

text.en: Supply rose sharply first, so sellers raised the price to slow buying.
Demand fell while supply also fell, so masks became costlier.
Sellers agreed on one high price, and buyers had no other choice.
Demand rose sharply, and supply could not keep up at first.

explanation.en: Demand rose much faster than makers could produce masks, so there was a shortage and the price rose. Later, supply rose and the price fell again.

hints.en: Which side of the market changed first? Could the other side change at once?
